newsitem.title: USA: United Tech CEO upbeat on auto business.
newsitem.headline: United Tech CEO upbeat on auto business.

text.p: United Technologies Corp Chief Executive George David said Tuesday he is "quietly confident" of improved earnings in the company's automotive unit.
"I feel actually quietly confident about long-term performance there," David told reporters after the company's annual shareholders meeting.
Automotive was one of the few disappointments when the Hartford-based company, whose products range from air conditioners to helicopters, reported its quarterly earnings last week.

"We did not think that 1997 was going to be a gangbusters year for UT Automotive," David said. "We think the first and second quarters may be weakish, and we'll get it back in the third and fourth quarters."
He said the business should continue to improve over the next two years, barring a dramatic downturn in the automotive industry.
"We have a new divisional president, we have some very interesting new car platforms and car launches and product innovations coming up."
David also said that United Technologies' jet engine unit Pratt & Whitney needed to work harder to become cost competitive against competitor General Electric Co.
"We are not yet cost competitive with General Electric. They do their volume of business with 5,000 fewer employees than we do."
He declined to comment on possible job cuts at Pratt.
David also said Asia will become a larger engine for the company's growth in the future. It now contributes about $5 billion, or one fifth, of United Technologies' total revenues.
"We need to increase the management presence in Asia, but it will not have an impact on the (450-employee) headquarters in Hartford," he said.
"The Asian theater is critically important to the future of the company."
Former U.S. Secretary of Defense William Perry was elected to the company's board of directors on Tuesday.
